findings.title: The mode factory omits a required checkpoint method
findings.claim: The stated complete ModeHost lifecycle leaves out synchronous checkpoint().
findings.why: A factory implementing the listed methods cannot satisfy ModeHost, and hostRuntime calls checkpoint() for a host command.
findings.fix: Add checkpoint(): Uint8Array to the factory contract and specify its bounded-byte behavior separately from async captureCheckpoint().

findings.title: EncounterRules cannot supply the duel tick to the generic core
findings.claim: The rules interface has no tick accessor, but the core repeatedly reads state.tick and DuelState has no top-level tick.
findings.why: The R-1 generic core cannot compile or publish a duel from the specified interface.
findings.fix: Define a tick(state) hook or an explicit common state constraint, and state how the duel interior and tactical ticks stay equal through step and restore.

findings.title: Duel completion has no specified wire record
findings.claim: terminal() returns an optional unknown endRecord, while the existing ended event requires a strict sector TelemetryRecord.
findings.why: Implementers must invent a duel completion payload or omit a required authority event; an arbitrary record fails the merged codec.
findings.fix: Define the common or mode-tagged ended-event type and codec, including the duel record and behavior when no end record exists.

findings.title: The duel snapshot format leaves restore rules undecided
findings.claim: The R-1 codec requirement names four areas but does not say which tactical and interior fields are stored, regenerated, or excluded, or how the encoded checkpoint stays within 256 KiB.
findings.why: Two implementations could restore the same immediate hash yet differ on later ticks, especially for seed-derived map/grid data and tactical random state.
findings.fix: Specify the snapshot header and field manifest, derived-field reconstruction and validation, post-restore continuation proof, and an encoded-size boundary test.

findings.title: The generic replay contract is unspecified
findings.claim: R-1 promises the Authority replay surface and preservation of V2/V3/V4 semantics, but the merged replay parser and runner require sector layout, checkpoint, snapshot, and message validation.
findings.why: A plan writer must decide whether duel replay is portable in R-1 and how its mode-specific data is validated before constructing state.
findings.fix: Define mode-aware replay parsing and restoration for the duel, and add an observable V2/V3/V4 replay check to R-1 acceptance.

findings.title: The R-1 history ring has no bound or proof
findings.claim: R-1 delivers a bounded ring, but the spec calls it only a small ring and gives no segment, byte, or export limit or acceptance check.
findings.why: Implementers must choose retention and failure behavior, and the stated R-1 proof cannot show that history remains bounded.
findings.fix: Set retention and byte limits, eviction and oversized-segment behavior, export scope, and a test that exceeds each bound.

findings.title: The unchanged-deps claim omits resolveLayout
findings.claim: The spec says the generic authority keeps the merged deps unchanged but its list omits required resolveLayout.
findings.why: R-1 implementers must guess whether layout resolution remains a dependency or moves into the rules and checkpoint codec.
findings.fix: Include resolveLayout in the retained sector deps, or explicitly assign layout resolution to EncounterRules and describe the sector adapter.

findings.title: Risk 3 understates deferred projection changes
findings.claim: Risk 3 says only image selection per connection is new, while §10 requires new metadata, client acceptance, event filtering, and a re-host checkpoint policy.
findings.why: The risk statement contradicts the deferred R-6 design and would understate its later scope.
findings.fix: Revise risk 3 to name those additional R-6 changes while keeping PvP deferred.
